# TriageIQ — Canonical Facts

Every number in every other document must match this file. If they disagree, this file wins.

## Why this file exists

Earlier documentation quoted statistics without saying *which population* they came from, so
all-time figures ended up standing in for windowed ones. There are **three populations** and they
are not interchangeable. Always state the frame.

| frame | what it is | rows |
|---|---|---|
| **F1 — feature population** | all complaints in the window. Loaded into Postgres. Aggregates computed here. | **4,826,564** |
| **F2 — modeling population** | F1 rows that have a narrative. Only these can be training rows. | **1,639,068** |
| **F3 — training artifact** | the shipped sampled parquet | **301,460** |

Window: 2022-01-01 .. 2024-12-31. Label: `Company response to consumer == 'Closed with monetary relief'`.

## Schema-critical facts

- `Complaint ID` unique across F1: **True** — safe primary key
- All numeric: **True**, range 5,059,826 .. 25,594,248 → store as **BIGINT** (stored as text in the CSV; text sort != numeric sort)
- Company-day groups: 280,846; **43.46% hold more than one complaint**; max **4,245** in one company-day
- NULL `Company response to consumer` in F1: **19** rows — these are *unknown*, not negative; exclude rather than label 0

## `Submitted via` — the column whose verdict flips by frame

- F2 (narrative rows): **1 distinct value** — dead for the model
- F1 (feature population): **5 distinct values** — Web 4,706,666, Phone 67,953, Referral 34,071, Postal mail 17,873, Email 1

Not information-free in F1. Dropping it from `fact_complaint` forfeits features like
"share of this company's complaints arriving by phone". Decide deliberately.

## Baselines — measured on F3, the data that actually ships

Reproduce with `training/verify_ablation.py`.

| model | pooled AUC | pooled PR | within (Product x Issue) AUC |
|---|---|---|---|
| text only | 0.9542 | 0.3551 | **0.8905** |
| metadata only | 0.9533 | 0.3414 | **0.9076** |
| **fusion** | **0.9634** | **0.4073** | **0.9330** |

> An earlier table quoted 0.898 / 0.940 / 0.945. Those came from a 500k random sample with a
> different split — **not** the shipped artifact. The target to beat is **0.9330**.
>
> The metadata branch loses 0.032 on F3 because target encoding was fitted on case-control-resampled
> train data (25% positive instead of ~3.4%), distorting both the rates and the smoothing prior.
> **Entity rates must be computed over F1 in Postgres, never over resampled training rows.**
